Subject: Data residency + retention requirements for PHI workloads

Hannah,

Thanks for taking a look. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will store and process PHI-derived embeddings and generated summaries. Before we proceed we'd like clarity on two things:

1) Can retention be configured per-customer and per-region (we require EU for EU patient data, US for US patient data)?
2) Do you provide an automated deletion workflow with verifiable audit trail (we need proof of deletion for periodic audits)?

Attached is a short Q&A and our initial compliance checklist. Happy to jump on a quick call but wanted to capture the asks in writing first.

— Sam Rivera
Head of Security, Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, we can support configurable retention policies that are applied per-tenant and scoping to a region.
- We have a deletion workflow that emits deletion audit records; we can provide a deletion proof artifact for each delete operation.

That said, the specific controls and the timeline for making per-region retention fully self-serve depend on whether you run on Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private.

To move this to a concrete plan, I'm looping in Karthik (product/arch), Dev (eng lead), and Marissa (customer success) to draft a short playbook for:
  • policy configuration UI/API surface
  • enforcement model (regional buckets vs. policy-based tagging)
  • deletion proof format and retention audit export
  • expected rollout timeline & impact on SLAs

Karthik/Dev/Marissa — can you review and propose next steps? Sam — if you have any constraints (encryption at rest key residency, KMS requirements, max retention windows), please send them over.

Best,
Hannah

Subject: Internal: Acme Health — roadmap request for regional retention + deletion playbook

Team —

Acme (potential pilot) asked for a formal "playbook" describing how we support: per-tenant regional retention, automated deletion with verifiable audit trail, and associated SLA implications. High level asks from the customer:
  1) Ability to pin retention by region and to prevent cross-region backups for data labeled as region-bound.
  2) A deletion API that returns an immutable proof (hash + timestamp + region) and an exportable audit report.
  3) A timeline for when we can make this self-serve (console + API) for Hosted customers; they also want clarity on Dedicated/Private behavior.

Constraints to flag in the playbook:
  - Need to avoid cross-region replication for data marked region-restricted.
  - Deletion must consider async caches (KV cache / prefix cache) and any long-lived artifacts (embeddings stored in vector DBs).
  - Key management: some customers will require customer-managed keys in-region (KMS/HSM).

Request: can you sketch a minimal implementation that covers Hosted + Dedicated, call out gaps for Private, and estimate engineering effort (S/M/L) and a rough timeframe (Q3 / Q4). Please attach any supporting notes or sample API shapes to the reply.

I attached a draft playbook template — feel free to edit. I want to get a short customer-facing doc by next Friday so we can share with Acme and Regula Consulting.

Thanks — Hannah
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Internal: Acme Health — roadmap request for regional retention + deletion playbook

Quick technical outline and tradeoffs: 

Option A — Region-tagged object storage + policy engine (low user friction).  • Store artifacts in region-scoped buckets; metadata includes tenant_id + retention_ttl + region_tag.  • Deletion = mark-for-delete + background scrub that removes objects and emits deletion-proof records.  • Pros: clear mapping to region; easier to satisfy regulatory audits.  • Cons: increased operational complexity (per-region bucket lifecycle), cross-region failover gets tricky.

Option B — Logical policies with cross-region replication disabled for region-restricted tenants (simpler storage model).  • Keep single global store but enforce replication rules and encryption key residency.  • Pros: simpler for HA/failover; easier reuse of existing infra.  • Cons: harder to prove physical deletion unless you pin objects to regional hardware.

Key engineering items to call out:
  - KV cache invalidation: need a coordinated purge across serving nodes to avoid rehydration after delete.
  - Embedding indexes: if embeddings are stored in vector DBs we must support tombstoning + background compaction to physically remove vectors.
  - Deletion proofs: we can produce signed statements (signed by Redwood KMS) including object digests and timestamps; need retention on the audit logs service (exportable CSV/JSON).

Effort estimate (MVP): 3-4 Sprints (core policy + deletion proof + console UI) for Hosted, assuming we reuse existing storage primitives. Dedicated will need a runbook and limited configuration surface (2 Sprints). Private depends on customer infra (TBD).

I'll open PLAT-987 and draft the API shapes. Attaching a short tech note.

—Karthik
Principal Product Architect
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 22 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme Health — roadmap request for regional retention + deletion playbook

Thanks — brief engineering follow-ups and gating items:

1) Storage mapping: we can implement Option A for Hosted by creating region-specific storage classes and lifecycle controllers. We'll need infra time to provision region buckets and CI templates (estimate: 2 Sprints infra + 2 Sprints service work).

2) KV cache invalidation: implement coordinated invalidation via our control plane streaming channel. Risk: short window where stale prefixes could be served; mitigation: immediate tombstone + synchronous cache purge for deletion API calls.

3) Embedding deletion: depends on vector-store choice. For our managed vector index we can support tombstones + background compaction. For customers that bring their own DBs we need documented runbooks.

4) Audit proof format: propose JSONL with signed digest entries and S3-stored proof bundle, plus a verification endpoint. We can reuse existing signing keys but customers asking for CMKs will need additional integration.

Deliverables and timeline proposal:
  - Week 1: PLAT-987 created + tech note + sample API shapes (in Jira).
  - Sprint 1-2 (Infra): region bucket automation & KMS config templates.
  - Sprint 3-4 (Service): policy engine, deletion API, proof generation, console UI.

I'll attach a short migration spreadsheet and region-mapping sample. Need CS to prioritize pilot customers and confirm which customers require CMKs.

—Dev Patel
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Sam — thanks, we put together a short playbook draft and a proposed timeline for an initial pilot. Key points: 
  • We can support per-tenant, per-region retention; for Hosted we plan a region-bucket approach with signed deletion proofs.
  • MVP timeline (Hosted): ~8 weeks (infra + service + UI). Dedicated: additional runbook + ~4 weeks of config work. Private: depends on customer infra; we will provide the playbook and an install checklist.
  • Gating items for your team: confirm whether Acme requires customer-managed keys (KMS) in-region; confirm list of datasets that must remain region-bound; confirm acceptable deletion-proof format (JSONL with signed digests).

Next steps:
  1) Sam — can you confirm KMS requirement and share a prioritized list of tenant datasets?
  2) Regula — can you review the attached playbook and highlight any audit gaps from a compliance perspective?
  3) We will schedule a technical walkthrough next week (30 min) to demo the deletion proof concept and show the sample API shapes (link below).
